about.title: Santa Maria Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Maria's workforce spends much of its day in fields, packing sheds, warehouses, construction sites, and behind the wheel. When a shift ends in an injury, the first worry is rarely about fault. It is about rent, medical bills, and whether the job will still be there. Under California law, workers' compensation normally covers you regardless of who caused the accident, and it is generally the only claim you can bring against your own employer. That is not always where the story ends, though. If a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a defective machine, or another driver played a role, a separate third-party injury claim may be available in addition to comp benefits. Driving for work is a real example in this city: Santa Maria recorded 412 injury collisions in 2025, with 562 people hurt, and public records show volume clustering along Broadway, Main Street, Blosser Road, and Donovan Road. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Maria Workers Use LawProactive

items.title: Two Claims, Not Just One
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party such as a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver can open a separate injury claim. An attorney in our network can tell you if that second door exists for you.

items.title: Your Report Is Protected
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and it is illegal for an employer to punish you for doing so. If you are worried about pushback, a lawyer can walk you through how to report safely and what to document.

items.title: Deadlines Handled Early
items.desc: Third-party injury claims in California carry a two-year filing deadline, and evidence from a job site or roadway does not wait around. Connecting sooner gives an attorney time to preserve what matters.

items.question: I was hit on Blosser Road while making deliveries for my employer. Is that a workplace injury or a car accident?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, the injury generally falls under workers' compensation regardless of who caused the collision. If the other driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver, which is a different process with its own two-year deadline. An attorney can review both tracks together so nothing is left on the table.

items.question: Can I be fired for reporting an injury on a Santa Maria job site?
items.answer: No. California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a workers' compensation claim. You should still report within 30 days to protect your benefits. If you experience threats, cut hours, or termination after reporting, that is something to raise with an attorney right away.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to get connected with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You can ask questions during the initial review without any obligation.
